protocol.name: ahmadi2019_id2m
protocol.method: Single-plate digital microfluidics (DMF) integrated with droplet-in-channel microfluidics for on-demand droplet generation, mixing, incubation, and n-ary sorting
protocol.reference: Ahmadi, Samlali, Vo, Shih. Lab Chip, 2019, 19, 524-535. DOI: 10.1039/c8lc01170b
protocol.target_organism: Fluorescein dye (Protocol 1, calibration); Saccharomyces cerevisiae BY4741 wild-type and EMS-mutagenized ionic-liquid-tolerant mutants (Protocol 2)
protocol.application: On-chip fluorescence calibration / dilution-series sorting, and yeast mutant library screening for ionic-liquid tolerance via n-ary droplet sorting

modules.description: Abstracts the on-chip optical-fibre fluorescence detection interface (530 nm strip-chart, 100 ms integration, boxcar smoothing width 3, 5 scans); used for the fluorescein calibration/dilution series
Abstracts the on-chip optical-fibre absorbance detection interface (boxcar smoothing width 2, 2 scans); used to measure cell density (OD) of incubated yeast/ionic-liquid droplets

reagents.description: Fluorescein (free acid) dissolved at 1 mM in 1 M NaOH buffer, pH 9; used as the analyte for the on-chip calibration dilution series
reagents.quantity_unit: units (~30 nL per on-demand T-junction droplet)

reagents.description: Diluent droplet (buffer or water) used to construct the 2x, 4x, and 8x fluorescein dilution series by sequential merging in the mixing area
reagents.quantity_unit: units (~30 nL per on-demand T-junction droplet)

reagents.description: 1-Ethyl-3-methylimidazolium acetate ionic liquid (IL), HPLC grade, >=95%; 200 mM stock merged 1:1 with a single-cell yeast droplet to yield a final on-chip concentration of 100 mM
reagents.quantity_unit: units (~35 nL per on-demand T-junction droplet)

reagents.description: Saccharomyces cerevisiae BY4741 wild-type cells (genotype: MATa his3D1 leu2D0 met15D0 ura3D0); Poisson-encapsulated as single cells via flow-focusing (2x10^5 cells/mL suspension + 1% BSA)
EMS-mutagenized ionic-liquid-tolerant yeast mutant #1 (fastest-growing isolate from random mutant library screened on 50/75/100 mM IL agar plates); Poisson-encapsulated as single cells
EMS-mutagenized ionic-liquid-tolerant yeast mutant #2 (second-fastest-growing isolate from random mutant library screened on 50/75/100 mM IL agar plates); Poisson-encapsulated as single cells

device_architecture.description: Three-layer microfluidic chip: a single-plate co-planar digital microfluidic (DMF) layer (104 patterned chromium electrodes on glass) bonded under a ~7 um SU-8 dielectric layer and a 110-120 um SU-8 channel layer (300 um wide), sealed with a ~0.5 mm PDMS slab carrying inlets/outlets. Combines pressure-driven droplet-in-channel flow with electrostatic droplet actuation on the same substrate, avoiding the droplet-transfer difficulties of separate droplet/digital microfluidic platforms.
device_architecture.actuation: 200 V_rms at 15 kHz; oil-phase (HFE7500 + 0.75% fluorosurfactant) flow rate in main channel: 0.01 uL/s; throughput ~1 Hz

device_architecture.description: Two bare optical fibres (100 um core, NA 0.22) inserted perpendicular to the main channel; one coupled to a 4-channel high-power LED source (470/530/590/627 nm), the other to a Flame spectrometer (Ocean Optics). Fibre-to-channel distance ~200 um. Fluorescence settings: 530 nm, 100 ms integration, boxcar width 3, 5 scans. Absorbance settings: boxcar width 2, 2 scans.

Symmetrical T-channel design with four sorting outlets per detection event (as opposed to typical binary Y-channel sorters, which create stagnation zones and asymmetric droplet resistance when expanded beyond two outlets). Droplets are biased directly to a sorting channel by electrode actuation after passing the optical detection region.

Multiple sink (side) channels added to the mixing area to create flow eddies and reduce local oil-phase hydrodynamic resistance, allowing droplets to be actuated from the main channel into the mixing region without being blocked by the higher resistance created by a droplet already occupying the mixing channel. Modelled by COMSOL Multiphysics V5.3 (single-phase laminar Navier-Stokes, oil density 1614 kg/m^3, dynamic viscosity 0.00124 Pa.s, inlet velocity 0.0003 m/s).

steps.name: Dispense undiluted fluorescein stock droplet for calibration check
steps.note: 1 mM fluorescein (in 1 M NaOH, pH 9) dispensed on-demand via T-junction (~30 nL); used directly as the highest-concentration calibration reference and is not consumed by any dilution step

steps.name: Generate 2x dilution droplet (0.5 mM)
steps.note: Fresh stock droplet merged 1:1 with one fresh on-demand buffer droplet in the mixing area (back-and-forth actuation, several seconds); (1 unit x 1 mM) / 2 units total = 0.5 mM

steps.name: Generate 4x dilution droplet (0.25 mM)
steps.note: Target: 1:3 dilution (1 unit stock + 3 units buffer = 4 units total, 0.25 mM). Compiler ignores multi-unit volume scalars (dispense 3 units defaults to 1 unit in IR); three buffer droplets explicitly instantiated and chain-merged into a single combined buffer droplet before the final mix with a fresh stock droplet. (1 unit x 1 mM) / 4 units total = 0.25 mM.

steps.name: Generate 8x dilution droplet (0.125 mM)
steps.note: Target: 1:7 dilution (1 unit stock + 7 units buffer = 8 units total, 0.125 mM); matches the paper's reported maximum 8x dilution of stock analyte given the device's minimal-inlet droplet-in-channel constraint. Seven buffer droplets explicitly instantiated and chain-merged before the final mix with a fresh stock droplet. Every variable is dispensed and consumed exactly once; no aliasing in IR.

steps.name: Fluorescence detection of all four calibration droplets
steps.note: Optical-fibre fluorescence interface (530 nm); each droplet detected independently as it passes the detection region prior to n-ary sorting. Detect consumes its fluid operand in this compiler -- a distinct downstream variable is used per detect call, not reused.

steps.name: Calibration QC gate, n-ary sort, and join cleanup
steps.note: QC gate keyed on the undiluted stock signal (expected highest, ~1900 a.u. sorting threshold per paper Fig. 3c). Pass: all four droplets exceed their respective sort thresholds (~1900/~1350/~950/~700 a.u.) and are routed to one of the four n-ary sorting channels (dispose models successful sort-and-collect). Fail: below the ~700 a.u. detection floor; routed to waste (drain). Both branches join before Protocol 2 begins.

steps.name: Poisson single-cell encapsulation of yeast droplets
steps.note: Flow-focusing encapsulation (2x10^5 cells/mL + 1% BSA, 0.0008 uL/s cells : 0.01 uL/s oil) generating ~35 nL droplets, one per cell type: wild-type and the two fastest-growing EMS-mutagenized IL-tolerant isolates

steps.name: On-demand T-junction generation of ionic-liquid droplets
steps.note: 200 mM IL stock, ~35 nL on-demand droplets; one IL droplet generated per single-cell droplet so that 1:1 merging yields a final on-chip concentration of 100 mM

steps.name: Merge each single-cell droplet with its ionic-liquid droplet
steps.note: Electrode actuation sequence (200 V_rms, 15 kHz) in the mixing area; produces a final 100 mM IL droplet containing a single yeast cell for each of the three conditions

steps.name: Trap and incubate at 30 C for 24 h
steps.note: Each merged droplet is actuated into one of the four on-chip incubation traps and held for 24 h at 30 C in a humidified chamber; heat is void in BioScript (no assignment) -- the reaction variables survive intact

steps.name: Post-incubation absorbance detection
steps.note: Optical-fibre absorbance interface measures cell density. Expected OD per paper Fig. 4: wild-type ~0.04-0.07 (no growth, indistinguishable from oil background), mutant #1 ~0.6, mutant #2 ~1.0

steps.name: IL-tolerance QC gate, n-ary sort, and final cleanup
steps.note: QC gate keyed on mutant #2 signal (expected highest absorbance/cell density). Pass: growth detected; all three droplets routed to their respective n-ary sorting channels by absorbance level for downstream analysis (e.g. single-cell sequencing). Fail: no growth signal above oil background; routed to waste (drain). Both branches join at the terminal block, where all signal droplets are disposed.
